cues.en: A war has been raging for billions of years, killing trillions every single day, while we don't even notice. The war is fought by the single deadliest entity on our planet, the bacteriophage, or phage for short. A phage is a virus, not quite alive, not quite dead. Also, they look as if someone made them up.
cues.zh: 一场战争已经持续了数十亿年，每天杀死数以万亿计的生命，而我们甚至毫无察觉。这场战争的参战者是地球上最致命的单一实体——噬菌体，简称 phage。噬菌体是一种病毒，算不上活着，也算不上死了。而且它们看起来就像是谁凭空编出来的。

cues.en: Their head is an icosahedron, a sort of dice with 20 faces and 30 edges. It contains the genetic material of the virus and often sits on a long tail that has leg-like fibres. There are more phages on Earth than every other organism combined, including bacteria. And they are probably everywhere living things exist. Billions are on your hands, in your intestines and your eyelids right now.
cues.zh: 它们的头部是一个二十面体，一种有20个面和30条棱的骰子。它装着病毒的遗传物质，通常连在一条长尾上，长尾带有腿状纤维。地球上的噬菌体数量超过所有其他生物的总和，连细菌也算在内。而且凡有生命存在的地方，可能都有它们。此刻，你手上、肠道里和眼睑上就有数十亿个。

cues.en: Which might make you nervous since phages are responsible for the majority of deaths on Earth. But you're lucky. While they do commit genocide for breakfast, they only kill bacteria. Up to 40% of all bacteria in the oceans are killed by them every single day. But phages also have major flaws. Like any other virus, phages need a host to survive and reproduce. They're not much more than genetic material in a hull, and they specialize.
cues.zh: 这可能会让你紧张，因为地球上大多数死亡都是噬菌体造成的。不过你运气不错。虽然它们把大屠杀当早餐，但只杀细菌。海洋中所有细菌里，每天有多达40%被它们杀死。但噬菌体也有重大缺陷。和其他病毒一样，噬菌体需要宿主才能生存和繁殖。它们不过是外壳里的一点遗传物质，而且高度专一。

cues.en: Usually, a phage has chosen one specific bacteria and maybe some of its very close relatives. These are its prey. Imagine a phage as like a cruise missile that only hunts and kills members of one very unlucky family. When a phage finds its victim, it connects its tail fibers with receptors and uses a sort of syringe to puncture the surface. In a weird motion, the phage squeezes its tail and injects its genetic information.
cues.zh: 通常，噬菌体会选定一种特定细菌，也许还有它的一些近亲。这些就是它的猎物。把噬菌体想象成一枚巡航导弹，只追猎并杀死某个非常不幸的家族成员。当噬菌体找到受害者时，它会将尾丝与受体结合，并用一种类似注射器的结构刺穿表面。以一种奇怪的动作，噬菌体挤压尾部，注入它的遗传信息。

cues.en: Within minutes, the bacteria is taken over. It's now forced to manufacture all the parts of new phages. They only stop when the bacteria is filled up with brand new phages. In the final step, they produce endolysin, a powerful enzyme that punches a hole in the bacteria. The pressure is so high that the bacteria sort of vomits out all of its insides and dyes. New phages are released and begin the cycle anew.
cues.zh: 几分钟内，细菌就被接管了。它现在被迫制造新噬菌体的所有部件。直到细菌被全新噬菌体填满，它们才会停止。最后一步，它们会产生内溶素，这是一种能在细菌上打孔的强大酶。压力高到细菌会像呕吐一样把内部物质全部排出，然后死亡。新噬菌体被释放出来，开始新一轮循环。

cues.en: In the last few years, bacteriophages have enjoyed the attention of the second deadliest beings on Earth, humans. Recently, we've started looking into injecting millions of them into our bodies, because we're sort of getting desperate. We screwed up. In the past, a single cut or a sip from the wrong puddle could kill you. Bacteria were our phages, tiny monsters that hunted us mercilessly. But then, about 100 years ago, we found a solution in nature.
cues.zh: 过去几年，噬菌体得到了地球上第二致命的生物——人类——的关注。最近，我们开始研究把数百万个噬菌体注入体内，因为我们有点走投无路了。我们搞砸了。过去，一道小伤口，或者从错误的水坑里喝一口，都可能要你的命。细菌曾是我们的噬菌体，是无情猎杀我们的微小怪物。但后来，大约100年前，我们在自然界中找到了解决方案。

cues.en: By accident we found fungi that produced a compound that killed bacteria, antibiotics. Suddenly we had a powerful super weapon. Antibiotics were so effective that we stopped thinking of bacteria as monsters. Only the old and weakest among us were killed by them. We used antibiotics more and more for less and less serious causes. We lost respect for the monsters and the weapon. But bacteria are living things that evolve and one by one
cues.zh: 我们偶然发现，真菌会产生一种能杀死细菌的化合物，也就是抗生素。突然间，我们就有了一件强大的超级武器。抗生素太有效了，以至于我们不再把细菌当成怪物。只有我们当中年老体弱的人才会被它们夺去生命。我们越来越多地使用抗生素，用来对付越来越轻微的病症。我们不再敬畏这些怪物，也不再敬畏这件武器。但细菌是活物，会进化，于是一个接一个

cues.en: they started to become immune against our weapons. This continued until we had created what are called superbugs, bacteria immune to almost everything we have. This immunity is spreading across the world as we speak. By 2050, superbugs could kill more humans a year than cancer. The days when a cut or bladder infection or a cough could kill you or your loved ones are coming back.
cues.zh: 它们开始对我们的武器产生免疫力。这种情况持续下去，直到我们制造出了所谓的超级细菌——几乎对我们现有的一切都免疫的细菌。就在我们说话这会儿，这种免疫力正在全世界蔓延。到2050年，超级细菌每年杀死的人可能比癌症还多。一个伤口、一次膀胱感染或一场咳嗽就能夺走你或亲人生命的时代，正在回来。

cues.en: In the US alone, more than 23,000 people die from resistant bacteria each year. But it turns out that phages, our tiny killer virus robots, could save us. We can inject them into our bodies to help cure infections. Hold on, how can injecting millions of viruses into an infection be a good idea? Phages are very, very specialized killers of bacteria.
cues.zh: 仅在美国，每年就有超过23,000人死于耐药细菌。但事实证明，噬菌体——这些微小的杀手病毒机器人——或许能拯救我们。我们可以把它们注入体内，帮助治愈感染。等等，往感染处注入数百万个病毒怎么会是个好主意？噬菌体是非常非常专一的细菌杀手。

cues.en: So specialized, in fact, that humans are completely immune to them. We are too different. We encounter billions of phages every day, and we just politely ignore each other. Antibiotics are like carpet bobbing, killing everything, even the good bacteria in our intestines that we don't want to harm. Phages are like guided missiles that only attack what they're supposed to. Wait a minute.
cues.zh: 事实上，它们专一到人类对它们完全免疫。我们差异太大了。我们每天都会遇到数十亿个噬菌体，而彼此只是礼貌地互不理会。抗生素就像地毯式轰炸，什么都杀，甚至包括我们肠道里不想伤害的有益细菌。噬菌体则像精确制导导弹，只攻击它们该攻击的目标。等一下。

cues.en: If we use phages to kill bacteria, won't bacteria develop ways of defending themselves? Well, it's more complex than that. Phages evolve too. There has been an arms race between them and bacteria for billions of years, and so far, they're doing great. This makes phages smart weapons that are constantly getting better at killing. But even if bacteria were to become immune against our phage, we still might be able to win. It turns out,
cues.zh: 如果我们用噬菌体来杀细菌，细菌难道不会进化出防御手段吗？嗯，情况比这更复杂。噬菌体也在进化。它们和细菌之间的军备竞赛已经持续了数十亿年，而到目前为止，它们表现得很好。这让噬菌体成为智能武器，杀伤力还在不断增强。但即使细菌对我们的噬菌体产生免疫，我们仍可能赢。事实证明，

cues.en: that in order to become resistant to even just a few species of phages, bacteria have to give up their resistance to antibiotics. We might be able to trap them in a catch-22. This has already been successfully tested with a patient who had no other hope left. The bacteria Pseudomonas aeruginosa, one of the most feared bacteria, infected the man's chest cavity. They are naturally resistant to most antibiotics
cues.zh: 为了对哪怕少数几种噬菌体产生抗性，细菌也不得不放弃对 antibiotic 的耐药性。我们或许能让它们陷入进退两难的困境。这已在一名别无希望的病人身上成功试验过。铜绿假单胞菌是最令人恐惧的细菌之一，它感染了这名男子的胸腔。它们天然对大多数抗生素耐药。

cues.en: and can even survive an alcoholic hand gel. After years of suffering, a few thousand fages were directly inserted into his chest cavity together with antibiotics the bacteria were immune to. After a few weeks, the infections had completely disappeared. Unfortunately, this treatment is still experimental and pharma companies are still reluctant to invest the necessary billions in a treatment that has no official approval yet. But things are finally changing.
cues.zh: 并且它甚至能在含酒精的洗手凝胶中存活。在多年遭受病痛折磨后，几千个噬菌体被直接注入他的胸腔，同时配合使用细菌已经耐药的抗生素。几周后，感染完全消失了。不幸的是，这种疗法仍处于实验阶段，制药公司仍不愿为一种尚未获得正式批准的疗法投入所需的数十亿美元。但情况终于开始改变。

cues.en: In 2016, the largest phage clinical trial to date began, and phages are getting more and more attention. And we better get used to it, because the era in which antibiotics have been our super weapon is drawing to a close. It might be a weird concept, but injecting the deadliest being on planet Earth directly into our bodies could save millions of lives. cues.zh: 2016年，迄今为止规模最大的噬菌体临床试验启动，噬菌体正受到越来越多关注。我们最好习惯这一点，因为抗生素作为我们超级武器的时代正接近尾声。这概念可能很奇怪，但把地球上最致命的生物直接注入我们体内，可能拯救数百万人的生命。本视频由比尔及梅琳达·盖茨基金会资助制作。
